calls.head: The Oilers like Michaels’s line against Couturier’s
calls.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Michaels’s line (Jones, Michaels and Frederic) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flyers’ fourth line is Barkey, Couturier and Acciari.

calls.head: Vladař’s hold on the Oilers won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Vladař has been a wall against the Oilers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Oilers finally get to him.

calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Flyers
calls.body: On depth, Philadelphia is near the top of the league, but Edmonton is the worst. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Flyers.

calls.beyond: Edmonton rides their top six more than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a short bench: the bottom six played 33% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 39% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Bouchard wins it in overtime
paras: Zach Hyman opened the scoring for the Oilers early in the second, and he scored again on the power play midway through the period to make it 2-0. Tyson Foerster got the Flyers on the board on the power play less than three minutes later. Travis Sanheim tied it 2-2 midway through the third, and the goal stood after the Oilers challenged for goalie interference. Evan Bouchard won it 47 seconds into overtime. The Flyers’ Rasmus Ristolainen was back in the lineup after missing seven games, and picked up an assist.

The Flyers had a little more of the play, but the Oilers made their chances count. Tristan Jarry made 30 saves for the Oilers, and Dan Vladař stopped 21 of 24 at the other end. The Oilers moved to 14-3-3 and climbed into first in the NHL in points, while the Flyers dropped to 5-10-6, slipping to seventh in the Metropolitan.
